lines.text: Unit 02 Spread of islam
Tax System
Structure of finance and taxing remained almost the same as that during the pious
caliphate. Caliph Umar Bin Abdul Aziz proposed a major revision of the rules and
principles of taxation in order to achieve uniformity. The caliph Hisham followed the
policies of Caliph Umar Bin Abdul Aziz and introduced the same tax reforms in Khurasan,
EgyptandMesopotamia.
Reasons Leading to theDownfall of theUmayyad Dynasty
The Umayyad caliphate collapsed in 750 AD after a rule of about 90 years. The last 30
years of the caliphate witnessed great opposition of the Abbasids. This was not the only
cause of downfall of the Umayyads but there were many other factors too that caused
their decline. Some of these factors are stated as under:
a) Lifestyle of Leaders
Some of the caliphs in this dynasty spent their lives in a lavish manner which repulsed
people. The groups which were against the regime, got benefit from this situation and
provoked people against this weakness of the Umayyads.
b)TheDisgraceoftheNobles
With the arrival of the new caliph,the administrators and nobles of the previous regime
weremaltreated.Great generals Musa BinNusayr, Muhammad Bin Qasim and Qutayba
BinMuslim weremaltreated bythe new caliph Suleman Bin Abdul Malik.This and such
other incidents destroyed thespirit of loyaltyfrom thekeyfigures.
C)Discrimination Against Mawalis (Non-Arab Muslims)
During the caliphate of the Umayyads,the Mawalis were treatedas second class citizens.
They were kept away from government positions.Heavy taxes on them caused great
social unrest and resulted in helping the rebellions against the Umayyads.
d)IgnoringScholarlyActivities
One of the issues that bore negative consequences for Umayyads was their neglect of
scholarly activities. The scholarly mawalis who were cornered by the Umayyads became
brain of the opposition and joined rebellions.
e) Internal Conflicts
Another important cause of decline of Umayad dynasty was their internal conflicts.
These conflicts mostly arose for the succession and power. Many provinces revolted.
These internal conflicts strengthened the rivals so much that within few years, whole
dynasty collapsed.
